prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of GLP-1 and its active peptide form that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: All six openings placed B021 first, but agreement in rank is not the argument. The argument is the length and clarity of the causal chain: incretin physiology (Holst), proglucagon processing and receptor biology (Drucker) and identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov) were basic-science findings that created the rationale for drugs now used at very large scale. Independent outcome trials show cardiovascular and renal benefit, so the interpretation is stable and the maturity concern that applies to cGAS-STING or TOR does not arise. A single-achievement prize with three basic-science laureates is the cleanest configuration, and it fits the will's language on a discovery of greatest benefit to humankind.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Priority for the active truncated GLP-1 peptide is contested, and Habener's group is not among the supplied names. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen is the natural fourth name for the drug-development step, and a three-person cap forces us to treat the prize as physiology rather than as the therapy, which some will find incomplete given that the public impact lies in the long-acting drugs. A second concern is that a prize this popular may be easier to defend than to defend precisely.

responses.point: For B033 (CAR-T), the CAR-specific decisive contributions belong to June and Sadelain, and Rosenberg's adoptive-cell-therapy work, though important, is less specific to engineered receptors.
responses.response: I agree that a June and Sadelain pair is more defensible than adding Rosenberg, and for a single-achievement prize I would not add him just to reach three. I am less sure than you that the pair resolves the credit problem. The chimeric receptor concept originates with Eshhar's group, which is outside the supplied names, so I rank B033 second but not as a clean attribution. My view is that it is a strong second part only if the committee accepts a prize that omits that origin.

responses.point: B042 (nusinersen) is a clean mechanism-to-therapy translation: Krainer's splicing work identified the ISS-N1 target and Bennett led the antisense chemistry, turning a fatal infant disease into a treatable one.
responses.response: This matches my own ranking (fourth). The splicing mechanism is close to my own research area, which is why I try to be strict: the case is strong for clinical effect and clarity, but the story is a platform one. The antisense platform and the SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) sit partly outside the credited names, and I would hesitate to prefer it to B021 or to a well-attributed CAR-T pair. I would keep it as a future candidate rather than push it into this year's configuration.

responses.point: B032 (TNF blockade) is a well-attributed two-person prize with more than twenty-five years of confirmation and is arguably overdue rather than premature.
responses.response: The attribution to Feldmann and Maini is indeed cleaner than for B021, and I take seriously that maturity is a strength. My reservation is conceptual rather than about merit: the TNF story is partly a clinical translation of biology identified by others (Old, Cerami, Beutler) and of antibody engineering done in industry. I therefore see it as a worthy alternative but one that is more exposed than GLP-1 to an objection about what the discovery was. I did not rank it in my own top eight, and I accept that this may reflect field distance from rheumatology, as you note your own.

responses.point: For B044 (optogenetics), channelrhodopsin discovery and neuronal implementation are distinct steps, and a workable set is Hegemann with Boyden and Deisseroth.
responses.response: I agree the six-name crowding is the main obstacle, but I disagree with the Boyden-Deisseroth-Hegemann set as the most defensible one: it omits Nagel, whose joint work with Hegemann established channelrhodopsin function, and I find that harder to explain than leaving out a neuronal implementer. I ranked B044 sixth because it is a methods prize with a contested allocation. It is a credible alternative but not a better one than B021.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can credit the active GLP-1 peptide to Mojsov alone without resolving the dispute with Habener.
Whether leaving out Knudsen is defensible if the prize is read as recognizing the therapy.
Whether a CAR-T prize can be fair without Eshhar.
Whether a two-part prize combining B021 with another achievement is warranted when B021 alone is strong.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. I co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén, who are not candidates here, and share Karolinska Institutet with them; I do not read this as a recusal issue. My own research (single-cell and RNA processing) bears most closely on B042, where I have no documented tie to Krainer or Bennett but note the topical closeness.
